title: Hitler becomes Chancellor
text:
President Paul von Hindenburg appoints Adolf Hitler Chancellor of a coalition government of the Nazi Party and German nationalists. Hitler was not elected directly: the Nazi Party had become the strongest party in the November 1932 Reichstag election with 33.1 percent, and the appointment followed arrangements among conservative circles around Franz von Papen.
The Nazis celebrate the day as the “seizure of power”. Within a few months they turn the republic into a dictatorship.

title: Reichstag fire
text: The Reichstag building is on fire. The very next day the “Reichstag Fire Decree” suspends key fundamental rights. Until 1945 it serves as the basis for arrests without trial; thousands of Communists and Social Democrats are taken into “protective custody”.

title: Last Reichstag election with several parties
text: Amid terror and obstruction of the opposition, the Nazi Party wins 43.9 percent of the vote and falls short of an absolute majority. Together with the DNVP, Hitler’s government has a narrow majority in the Reichstag.

title: Dachau concentration camp established
text: One of the first concentration camps is set up near Munich, initially for political opponents. Dachau becomes the model for the later SS camp system. Until 1945 more than 200,000 people are held here, and more than 41,000 die.

title: Enabling Act
text: The Reichstag passes the “Law to Remedy the Distress of People and Reich” in the Kroll Opera House. Only the Social Democrats vote against; the Communist seats had already been suppressed. The government can now pass laws without parliament – the Weimar Constitution is effectively nullified.

title: Boycott of Jewish businesses
text: SA men stand in front of Jewish shops, medical practices and law offices. A few days later the “Law for the Restoration of the Professional Civil Service” follows, forcing Jewish and politically undesirable civil servants out of office.

title: Book burning
text: Students burn works by Jewish, pacifist and politically unwanted authors on Berlin’s Opernplatz and in many university towns, including Heinrich Mann, Erich Kästner, Kurt Tucholsky and Sigmund Freud.

title: Nazi Party becomes the only permitted party
text: After the ban on the Social Democrats and the self-dissolution of the other parties, the “Law against the Formation of New Parties” prohibits every political organisation except the Nazi Party. Germany is a one-party state.
wiki: Law Against the Formation of Parties

title: Reich Concordat with the Vatican
text: The German Reich and the Holy See regulate their relationship in a treaty. For the Nazi regime it means international recognition; the Catholic Church receives assurances for pastoral care and schools, which are soon violated.

title: Haavara Agreement
text: The Reich Ministry of Economics and Zionist organisations agree that Jewish emigrants to Palestine may take part of their assets with them in the form of German export goods. By 1939 around 60,000 German Jews emigrate to Palestine; the Jewish population of the Mandate grows sharply in the 1930s.

title: Withdrawal from the League of Nations
text: Hitler announces Germany’s withdrawal from the disarmament conference and the League of Nations. A referendum in November confirms the step with a staged majority of over 95 percent.

title: German–Polish non-aggression pact
text: Germany and Poland commit to renouncing force for ten years. The treaty breaks through the French alliance system in Eastern Europe. Hitler denounces it in April 1939.

title: Austrian Civil War
text: The Social Democratic Schutzbund rises against the authoritarian government of Engelbert Dollfuss. The army and the Heimwehr crush the uprising, using artillery against Viennese municipal housing blocks. Social democracy is banned, and Austria becomes an authoritarian corporatist state.

title: “Röhm Putsch”: murders of SA leadership and opponents
text: On Hitler’s orders the SS and Gestapo murder the SA leadership around Ernst Röhm as well as conservative opponents such as Kurt von Schleicher and Gustav von Kahr – at least 90, probably more than 150 people. A retroactive law declares the murders “state self-defence”.

title: July Putsch in Vienna, Dollfuss murdered
text: Austrian Nazis occupy the Federal Chancellery and shoot Chancellor Engelbert Dollfuss. The putsch fails; Mussolini has troops deployed at the Brenner Pass as a deterrent. Kurt Schuschnigg becomes Chancellor.

title: Hitler becomes “Führer and Reich Chancellor”
text: After Hindenburg’s death Hitler combines the offices of Reich President and Reich Chancellor. The same day the Reichswehr is sworn in to him personally. A referendum on 19 August confirms the step with almost 90 percent.

title: Soviet Union joins the League of Nations
text: Under People’s Commissar Maxim Litvinov the Soviet Union seeks cooperation with the Western powers against the growing danger from Nazi Germany (“collective security”).

title: Saar plebiscite
text: After 15 years of League of Nations administration, 90.7 percent of voters in the Saar territory vote for a return to the German Reich. The reintegration takes place on 1 March 1935 – a propaganda success for the regime.

title: Conscription reintroduced
text: In open breach of the Treaty of Versailles the Reich reintroduces conscription and announces an army of 36 divisions. The Reichswehr is now called the Wehrmacht. Britain and France merely protest.

title: Stresa Conference
text: Britain, France and Italy reaffirm Austria’s independence and condemn German rearmament. The “Stresa Front” soon falls apart, however, when Italy attacks Abyssinia.

title: Anglo-German Naval Agreement
text: Britain grants Germany a fleet of 35 percent of British tonnage, thereby accepting rearmament contrary to the Treaty of Versailles – without consulting France.

title: Nuremberg Laws
text: At the Nazi Party rally the Reichstag proclaims the “Reich Citizenship Law” and the “Law for the Protection of German Blood”. Jews lose their political rights, and marriages and relationships with “Germans of German blood” are banned. The laws create the legal basis for further exclusion.

title: Italy invades Abyssinia
text: Italian troops invade the Empire of Abyssinia from Eritrea and Italian Somaliland. Italy also uses poison gas. The League of Nations imposes half-hearted sanctions without an oil embargo – proof of its impotence.

title: End of the Long March
text: After about a year and thousands of kilometres, the remnants of the Chinese Red Army reach northern Shaanxi. During the march Mao Zedong establishes himself as the leading figure of the Communist Party.

title: Death of Izz ad-Din al-Qassam
text: British police kill the preacher who had built up an armed underground group in northern Palestine against the Mandate power and Zionist settlement. He becomes a symbol of Arab resistance; the armed wing of Hamas is later named after him.

title: Entry into the demilitarised Rhineland
text: German troops march into the Rhineland, demilitarised under the Treaty of Versailles and the Locarno Treaty. France and Britain do not respond militarily. Hitler’s risk-taking pays off once again.

title: Arab Revolt in Palestine
text: Riots in Jaffa and a six-month general strike begin an uprising of the Arab population against the British Mandate power and Jewish immigration. Britain suppresses it by 1939; several thousand Arabs and several hundred Jews and Britons are killed, and the Arab leadership is shattered afterwards.

title: Italy conquers Addis Ababa
text: Italian troops occupy the capital, and Emperor Haile Selassie goes into exile. On 9 May Mussolini declares the King of Italy Emperor of Ethiopia; the country is united with Eritrea and Somaliland to form “Italian East Africa”.

title: Military coup: start of the Spanish Civil War
text: Generals around Francisco Franco rise against the government of the Second Spanish Republic. The coup fails in Madrid and Barcelona, and an almost three-year civil war follows. Germany and Italy support the putschists, the Soviet Union the Republic; International Brigades fight on the Republican side.

title: Olympic Games in Berlin
text: The regime uses the Games for self-promotion and tones down visible antisemitic agitation for their duration. The African-American athlete Jesse Owens wins four gold medals.

title: First Moscow show trial – start of the Great Terror
text: The trial of Zinoviev and Kamenev begins a series of show trials. In the “Great Terror” of 1936–1938 Stalin has around 680,000 people shot on NKVD orders, and hundreds of thousands more end up in the Gulag camps. The leadership of the Red Army is also largely destroyed.

title: Rome–Berlin Axis
text: Germany and Italy agree on close cooperation. Shortly afterwards Mussolini speaks of an “axis” around which Europe would revolve – the term “Axis powers” is born.

title: Anti-Comintern Pact
text: Germany and Japan conclude an agreement against the Communist International. Italy joins in 1937. Politically the pact is directed against the Soviet Union.

title: Bombing of Guernica
text: The German “Condor Legion” and the Italian air force bomb the Basque town. Hundreds of civilians die. Pablo Picasso’s painting “Guernica” makes the attack a worldwide symbol of terror against civilians.

title: Japan begins the war against China
text: A clash between Japanese and Chinese troops at the Marco Polo Bridge escalates into open war. By the end of 1938 Japan conquers large parts of northern and eastern China. The Second Sino-Japanese War later becomes part of the Second World War.

title: Peel Commission proposes partition
text: A British commission of inquiry considers the Mandate unworkable and proposes partition for the first time: a small Jewish state in the north and along the coast, an Arab state united with Transjordan, and a British zone around Jerusalem with a corridor to the sea. The Zionist leadership is divided, the Arab side rejects it; the revolt flares up again.

title: Battle of Shanghai
text: In one of the largest battles of the war, Chinese troops defend Shanghai for three months with heavy losses. After the fall of the city the Japanese advance on the capital, Nanjing.

title: Hossbach Memorandum
text: Before the leadership of the armed forces and Foreign Minister von Neurath, Hitler sets out his plans to gain “living space”, first by absorbing Austria and Czechoslovakia. The minutes are regarded as evidence of the planned war of aggression.

title: Nanjing Massacre
text: After the conquest of the Chinese capital, Japanese soldiers murder prisoners of war and civilians for weeks and rape tens of thousands of women. Estimates of the number of victims range from several tens of thousands to over 200,000.

title: “Anschluss” of Austria
text: German troops march into Austria without resistance, and on 13 March the country is annexed to the German Reich by law. On 15 March Hitler speaks on Vienna’s Heldenplatz. Arrests and violent attacks on Jews begin immediately.

title: Évian Conference on refugees
text: Representatives of 32 states discuss taking in Jewish refugees from Germany and Austria. Almost all refuse to raise their admission quotas.

title: Munich Agreement
text: Hitler, Mussolini, Chamberlain and Daladier decide, without Czechoslovak participation, to cede the Sudetenland to the German Reich. The Wehrmacht occupies the area from 1 to 10 October. Chamberlain speaks of “peace for our time”; Czechoslovakia loses its border fortifications.

title: First Vienna Award
text: Germany and Italy award Hungary the south of Slovakia and of Carpathian Ukraine. Poland had already occupied the Olza region around Teschen in October.

title: November pogroms
text: In an act of violence orchestrated by the regime, synagogues are set on fire throughout the Reich and Jewish shops and homes are wrecked. Hundreds of people are murdered or driven to their deaths, and about 30,000 Jewish men are deported to concentration camps. The pogroms mark the transition from discrimination to open violence.

title: Kindertransport to Britain
text: By the outbreak of war around 10,000 mostly Jewish children from Germany, Austria, Czechoslovakia and Poland reach Britain without their parents. Many never see their families again.

title: Occupation of Prague – dismemberment of Czechoslovakia
text: One day after Slovakia’s declaration of independence, forced by Berlin, the Wehrmacht occupies Bohemia and Moravia, which is declared a “Protectorate”. Hungary annexes Carpathian Ukraine. For the first time Hitler conquers non-German-speaking territory – the policy of appeasement has failed.

title: Memel Territory to the German Reich
text: Under German pressure Lithuania cedes the Memel Territory, which had belonged to Lithuania since 1923. Hitler gives a speech in Memel.

title: British–French guarantee to Poland
text: Prime Minister Chamberlain declares that Britain and France would assist Poland in the event of an attack. The guarantee marks the end of the policy of appeasement.

title: End of the Spanish Civil War
text: After the fall of Madrid, Franco declares the war over. Hundreds of thousands of dead, mass flight and repression mark the toll; Spain remains a dictatorship until 1975.

title: Italy occupies Albania
text: Italian troops land on the Albanian coast, and King Zog flees. Albania is joined to Italy in a personal union and in 1940 serves as a staging area for the attack on Greece.

title: Battles of Khalkhin Gol
text: Soviet and Mongolian troops under Georgy Zhukov defeat the Japanese Kwantung Army in a border conflict. Japan subsequently turns away from plans against the Soviet Union and directs its expansion southwards.

title: British White Paper on Palestine
text: Britain limits Jewish immigration to 75,000 people over five years, restricts land purchases and holds out the prospect of a majority-Arab state within ten years. For Jews fleeing Nazi persecution an important refuge is thereby closed; the Zionist movement increasingly turns against Britain.

title: Pact of Steel
text: Germany and Italy conclude a military alliance obliging both to mutual assistance, even in a war of aggression.

title: Hitler–Stalin Pact
text: Foreign Ministers Ribbentrop and Molotov sign a non-aggression treaty. A secret additional protocol divides Eastern Europe into spheres of interest: eastern Poland, Finland, Estonia, Latvia and Bessarabia fall to the Soviet Union. The pact opens the way for Hitler to attack Poland.

title: Invasion of Poland – start of the Second World War
text:
Without a declaration of war the Wehrmacht attacks Poland. The battleship “Schleswig-Holstein” shells the Westerplatte, and the Luftwaffe destroys the small town of Wieluń. Danzig is incorporated into the Reich the same day.
Behind the front, SS and police Einsatzgruppen murder tens of thousands of members of the Polish elite and Jews.

title: Britain and France declare war
text: After their ultimatums expire, Britain and France declare war on the German Reich. No effective offensive in the West follows – until May 1940 the “Phoney War” prevails.

title: Soviet Union invades eastern Poland
text: In accordance with the secret additional protocol to the Hitler–Stalin Pact, the Red Army occupies the eastern half of Poland. In November the territories are attached to the Ukrainian and Belarusian Soviet Republics; hundreds of thousands of Poles are deported in the following months.

title: Fall of Warsaw and German–Soviet border treaty
text: Warsaw capitulates after heavy bombardment. The same day Germany and the Soviet Union fix the border of their occupation zones along the Pisa, Narew, Bug and San rivers; Lithuania falls into the Soviet sphere of interest.

title: General Government established
text: The western part of Poland is incorporated into the Reich (Wartheland, Danzig–West Prussia, East Upper Silesia), the rest becomes the “General Government” under Hans Frank, based in Kraków. The Polish population is deprived of rights, expelled and forced into labour.

title: Georg Elser’s assassination attempt on Hitler
text: The carpenter Georg Elser has single-handedly hidden a bomb in a pillar of the Bürgerbräukeller. Hitler leaves the hall 13 minutes before the explosion. Elser is murdered in Dachau concentration camp in 1945.

title: Winter War
text: The Soviet Union attacks Finland. Despite being outnumbered, the Finnish army resists for months. In the Moscow Peace Treaty Finland has to cede Karelia with Vyborg and further territories, but remains independent.

title: Battle of the River Plate
text: British cruisers engage the pocket battleship “Admiral Graf Spee”. She puts into Montevideo damaged and is scuttled by her own crew on 17 December.

title: “Aktion T4” killings of the sick
place: Grafeneck and five other killing centres
text: In Grafeneck the systematic murder of people with disabilities and mental illness in gas chambers begins. Until the official halt in August 1941 over 70,000 people are killed; the decentralised killings continue. Personnel and methods are later used in the extermination camps.

title: Katyn massacre
text: The Soviet NKVD shoots around 22,000 Polish officers, police officers and members of the intelligentsia in the Katyn Forest and elsewhere. The Soviet Union denies the crime until 1990 and blames the Germans.

title: Occupation of Denmark and attack on Norway
text: In “Operation Weserübung” the Wehrmacht occupies Denmark almost without a fight and lands in Norway. After two months of fighting Norway capitulates; the king and government go to London. For Germany the occupation secures the supply of ore from Sweden.

title: Western campaign begins – Churchill becomes Prime Minister
text: The Wehrmacht attacks the neutral Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg. The main thrust comes by surprise through the Ardennes and breaks through the French front at Sedan on 13 May. The same day Winston Churchill becomes British Prime Minister.

title: Bombing of Rotterdam
text: German bombers destroy Rotterdam’s city centre, and around 800 people die. Under threat of further attacks the Netherlands capitulates the next day; the queen and government have fled to London.

title: Evacuation of Dunkirk
text: Over 330,000 British and French soldiers are rescued from the Dunkirk pocket across the English Channel – also with hundreds of civilian boats. Britain thus manages to preserve most of its army.

title: Italy enters the war
text: Mussolini declares war on France and Britain when France’s defeat is foreseeable. The Italian offensive in the Western Alps remains almost entirely unsuccessful.
wiki: Military history of Italy during World War II

title: German troops occupy Paris
text: The French government has evacuated the capital and declared Paris an open city. The Wehrmacht marches in without a fight.

title: Soviet Union occupies the Baltics
text: After ultimatums the Red Army marches into Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia. “People’s parliaments” elected under Soviet control apply for admission to the USSR, which is carried out in early August 1940. Many Western states never recognise the annexation.

title: Armistice of Compiègne
text: In the same railway carriage in which Germany had to capitulate in 1918, France signs the armistice. The north and the Atlantic coast are occupied by Germany; in the south the Vichy regime under Marshal Pétain governs. Alsace-Lorraine is de facto annexed. From London General de Gaulle calls for resistance.

title: Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina to the USSR
text: After an ultimatum Romania cedes Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina to the Soviet Union. The Moldavian Soviet Republic is formed from them.
wiki: Soviet occupation of Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina

title: Battle of Britain
text: The Luftwaffe tries to gain air superiority over southern England as a precondition for an invasion. The Royal Air Force holds its ground; Hitler postpones the planned landing indefinitely. From September the Luftwaffe bombs London and other cities (“The Blitz”).

title: Pétain granted full powers – the Vichy regime
text: The French National Assembly grants Marshal Philippe Pétain full powers. The “État français”, seated in the spa town of Vichy, collaborates with Germany and enacts its own antisemitic laws.

title: Second Vienna Award
text: Germany and Italy divide Transylvania: the north with Cluj and the Székely Land goes to Hungary. Romania must also cede Southern Dobruja to Bulgaria. King Carol II abdicates, and General Antonescu takes power.

title: Tripartite Pact
text: Germany, Italy and Japan agree on mutual assistance should one of them be attacked by a power not yet involved – meaning the USA. Hungary, Romania, Slovakia, Bulgaria and Croatia join.

title: Italy attacks Greece
text: Italy attacks Greece from Albania. The Greek army repels the attack and advances into Albania – an embarrassment for Mussolini that leads to German intervention in spring 1941.

title: Bombing of Coventry
text: A large-scale night raid by the Luftwaffe destroys Coventry’s city centre and cathedral, and around 570 people die. Nazi propaganda coins the word “to coventrate”.

title: Warsaw Ghetto sealed off
text: Around 400,000 Jews are shut into a walled district. Hunger and epidemics kill tens of thousands by 1942; most inhabitants are murdered in the Treblinka extermination camp in 1942.

title: Sinking of the “Patria”
text: To prevent the deportation of Jewish refugees to Mauritius, the Jewish underground organisation Haganah attaches an explosive charge to the ship. The charge is too powerful, and the ship sinks in the harbour; around 260 people die.

title: Rommel and the Afrika Korps in Tripoli
text: After heavy Italian defeats against the British in Libya, Hitler sends an expeditionary corps under Erwin Rommel to North Africa. It pushes the British back to the Egyptian border.

title: Lend-Lease Act
text: The still neutral USA approves extensive deliveries of weapons and materiel to Britain, later also to the Soviet Union and China. President Roosevelt speaks of the “arsenal of democracy”.

title: Attack on Yugoslavia and Greece
text: After a pro-British coup in Belgrade the Wehrmacht and its allies attack Yugoslavia and Greece; an air raid on Belgrade kills thousands. Yugoslavia capitulates on 17 April and is dismembered; Greece is conquered by the end of April and divided into three occupation zones.

title: Proclamation of the “Independent State of Croatia”
text: Under German and Italian protection the fascist Ustaša under Ante Pavelić sets up a state that also includes Bosnia and Herzegovina. The regime murders hundreds of thousands of Serbs, Jews and Roma, including in the Jasenovac camp.

title: Battle of Crete
text: German paratroopers, at high cost, conquer the island defended by British, Australian, New Zealand and Greek troops.

title: Invasion of the Soviet Union
text: With over three million soldiers and allies Germany attacks the Soviet Union. The war is planned from the start as a war of annihilation: the “Commissar Order” prescribes murders, and millions of Soviet prisoners of war die of starvation. Behind the front, Einsatzgruppen systematically murder Jews.

title: Finland enters the war against the Soviet Union
text: After Soviet air raids Finland begins the “Continuation War” on Germany’s side and reconquers the territories ceded in 1940.

title: Mass shootings at Ponary
text: In a forest area near Vilnius, German units and Lithuanian collaborators shoot around 100,000 people by 1944, most of them Jews.

title: Atlantic Charter
text: Aboard a warship Roosevelt and Churchill formulate common goals for the post-war order: no territorial gains, self-determination of peoples, freedom of the seas. The Charter becomes the basis of the United Nations.

title: Siege of Leningrad
text: German and Finnish troops encircle Leningrad. The Wehrmacht is not meant to conquer the city but to starve it. In just under 900 days around a million civilians die, most of them of hunger. Supplies arrive only across the frozen Lake Ladoga.

title: Babyn Yar massacre
text: A unit of Einsatzgruppe C, supported by police and the Wehrmacht, shoots 33,771 Jews from Kyiv in two days. It is one of the largest single massacres of the Holocaust; by 1943 tens of thousands more are murdered at Babyn Yar.

title: Battle of Moscow
text: In December, in frost and with exhausted troops, the offensive on Moscow gets stuck a few dozen kilometres from the city. On 5 December the Soviet counter-offensive begins and throws the Wehrmacht back – the Blitzkrieg against the Soviet Union has failed.

title: Attack on Pearl Harbor
text: Japanese carrier aircraft attack the US Pacific Fleet; over 2,400 Americans die. At the same time Japan attacks Malaya, Hong Kong, the Philippines and Guam. The USA enters the war.

title: Chełmno extermination camp begins killing
text: In the first extermination camp the SS murders people in gas vans, at first Jews from the Wartheland, later also Roma from the Litzmannstadt ghetto. In total at least 150,000 people are killed here.

title: Germany declares war on the USA
text: Four days after Pearl Harbor, Germany and Italy declare war on the United States. The European and Asian wars merge into a world war.
wiki: German declaration of war on the United States

title: Hong Kong surrenders
text: After 18 days of fighting the British garrison surrenders. Hong Kong remains under Japanese occupation until August 1945.

title: Wannsee Conference
text: Chaired by Reinhard Heydrich, senior officials from ministries, the party and the SS coordinate the deportation and murder of Europe’s Jews, which they call the “Final Solution of the Jewish Question”. The minutes name eleven million people as the target.

title: Fall of Singapore
text: Around 80,000 British, Indian and Australian soldiers surrender to a smaller Japanese army – Churchill calls it the worst defeat in British history. By March Japan also conquers the Dutch East Indies and Rangoon.

title: Sinking of the “Struma”
text: The refugee ship with around 780 Jews from Romania is towed into the Black Sea after weeks of being held in Istanbul and sunk by a Soviet submarine; only one passenger survives. Britain had refused entry to Palestine.

title: Auschwitz-Birkenau becomes the centre of the genocide
text: From spring 1942 deportation trains from all over Europe arrive at Auschwitz-Birkenau. On arrival the SS immediately selects most people for the gas chambers. By 1945 around 1.1 million people are murdered in Auschwitz, about a million of them Jews.

title: Operation Reinhard: extermination camps Bełżec, Sobibór, Treblinka
text: At Bełżec the murder of the Jews of the General Government in gas chambers begins; Sobibór and Treblinka follow. By autumn 1943 about 1.7 million people are murdered in the three camps.

title: Biltmore Programme
text: At a conference in New York the Zionist movement openly demands for the first time a “Jewish Commonwealth” in all of Palestine and unrestricted immigration.

title: Battle of Midway
text: The US Navy sinks four Japanese aircraft carriers. Japan loses the initiative in the Pacific; the battle is regarded as the turning point of the Pacific War.

title: Lidice massacre
text: In reprisal for the assassination of Reinhard Heydrich in Prague, SS and police shoot all 173 men of the village, deport the women and children and raze the village to the ground.

title: Deportations from the Warsaw Ghetto to Treblinka
text: In eight weeks the SS deports around 250,000 people from the Warsaw Ghetto to the Treblinka extermination camp, where almost all are murdered immediately.

title: Guadalcanal campaign
text: With the landing of US Marines the first major Allied offensive in the Pacific begins. After six months of costly fighting on land, at sea and in the air, Japan evacuates the island.

title: Battle of Stalingrad
text: The 6th Army enters the city on the Volga, which is destroyed in months of house-to-house fighting. In November the Red Army encircles around 300,000 soldiers in “Operation Uranus”. On 2 February 1943 the last remnants surrender; only about 6,000 of the 91,000 prisoners return home after the war. Stalingrad is regarded as the psychological turning point of the war.

title: Second Battle of El Alamein
text: The British 8th Army under Bernard Montgomery breaks through the German–Italian positions west of Alexandria. Rommel’s Panzer Army has to retreat through Libya as far as Tunisia.

title: Allied landings in North Africa
text: American and British troops land in French Morocco and Algeria. After brief fighting, the Vichy troops in North Africa switch to the Allied side.

title: Occupation of southern France
text: In response to the landings in North Africa, German and Italian troops occupy the hitherto unoccupied zone of France. The French fleet scuttles itself at Toulon on 27 November.

title: Auschwitz Decree: deportation of Sinti and Roma
text: Heinrich Himmler orders the deportation of Sinti and Roma from the Reich to Auschwitz. Most of the roughly 23,000 deportees die in the Birkenau “Gypsy camp”; on the night of 2–3 August 1944 the SS murders the last more than 4,000 prisoners. In total up to 500,000 Sinti and Roma fall victim to the genocide.

title: Casablanca Conference
text: Roosevelt and Churchill decide to continue the war until the unconditional surrender of Germany, Italy and Japan, and agree on the landing in Sicily.

title: Sportpalast speech: “Do you want total war?”
text: After the defeat at Stalingrad, Propaganda Minister Joseph Goebbels calls for “total war” before a hand-picked audience. The speech is meant to prepare the population for further sacrifices.

title: Execution of members of the White Rose
text: Four days after their arrest while distributing leaflets at Munich University, Sophie and Hans Scholl and Christoph Probst are sentenced to death by the People’s Court and executed.

title: Warsaw Ghetto Uprising
text: When the SS wants to clear the ghetto for good, Jewish fighters of the ŻOB and ŻZW put up armed resistance for almost four weeks. The SS burns the ghetto down; more than 50,000 survivors are deported to camps.

title: Axis surrender in Tunisia
text: Around 250,000 German and Italian soldiers are taken prisoner. The war in Africa is over; North Africa becomes the starting point for the attack on Italy.

title: Battle of Kursk
text: The last major German offensive in the East fails against deeply echeloned Soviet defensive positions. Afterwards the initiative on the Eastern Front lies definitively with the Red Army.

title: Allied landings in Sicily
text: American and British troops land on Sicily. On 25 July the Fascist Grand Council deposes Mussolini, and the king has him arrested.

title: Firestorm in Hamburg
text: British and American bombers attack Hamburg repeatedly. On the night of 27–28 July a firestorm develops; in total around 34,000 people die.
wiki: Bombing of Hamburg in World War II

title: Italian armistice – German occupation
text: Italy concludes an armistice with the Allies. The Wehrmacht occupies northern and central Italy as well as the Italian zones in the Balkans and disarms the Italian army; hundreds of thousands of soldiers are deported as military internees for forced labour. In the north the “Italian Social Republic” arises under Mussolini.

title: Sobibór uprising
text: Prisoners kill several SS men, and around 300 manage to escape. Shortly afterwards the SS dissolves the camp. There had already been an uprising in Treblinka in August.

title: Tehran Conference
text: Stalin, Roosevelt and Churchill meet for the first time. They agree on the landing in France for 1944 and agree in principle on a westward shift of Poland.

title: German occupation of Hungary
text: To prevent its ally from switching sides, the Wehrmacht occupies Hungary. Immediately afterwards preparations begin for the deportation of Hungary’s Jews.

title: Deportation of Hungarian Jews to Auschwitz
text: In less than two months the Hungarian gendarmerie and the Eichmann unit deport around 437,000 people to Auschwitz-Birkenau, where most are murdered immediately.

title: Normandy landings (D-Day)
text: With over 150,000 soldiers on the first day, Allied troops land on five sections of the Normandy coast. The second front against Germany is opened; by the end of August the Allies are in Paris.

title: Oradour-sur-Glane massacre
text: A unit of the Waffen-SS division “Das Reich” murders 643 inhabitants of the French village, women and children in the burning church.

title: Operation Bagration
text: Exactly three years after the German invasion, the Red Army destroys Army Group Centre – the Wehrmacht’s worst defeat. Within a few weeks the front advances to the Vistula and East Prussia.

title: 20 July plot
text: Colonel Claus Schenk Graf von Stauffenberg detonates a bomb at the “Wolf’s Lair”; Hitler is only slightly injured. The coup attempt in Berlin fails. Stauffenberg and fellow conspirators are shot that same night, hundreds more are executed.

title: Warsaw Uprising
text: The Polish Home Army rises against the German occupation in order to liberate Warsaw itself before the Red Army arrives. The Soviets halt on the other bank of the Vistula. After 63 days the insurgents capitulate; around 150,000 civilians die, and the city is then systematically destroyed.

title: Romania switches sides
text: King Michael has dictator Ion Antonescu arrested; Romania declares war on Germany. The German southern front collapses, and the Red Army advances rapidly into Bulgaria and Hungary.

title: Liberation of Paris
text: After an uprising by the Resistance, French and American troops enter Paris. The German city commander surrenders without carrying out the order to destroy the city. General de Gaulle forms a provisional government.

title: Operation Market Garden
text: A large-scale airborne operation is meant to seize the Rhine bridges in the Netherlands and open the way to the Ruhr. It fails at Arnhem.

title: Aachen captured as the first major German city
text: After weeks of fighting, the German garrison of the largely destroyed city surrenders to American troops.

title: Battle of Leyte Gulf
text: In the largest naval battle in history the Japanese fleet is decisively defeated. For the first time Japan uses kamikaze pilots. The reconquest of the Philippines begins.

title: Assassination of Lord Moyne
text: Members of the radical Jewish underground group Lehi shoot the British Minister for the Middle East in Cairo. The Haganah then temporarily takes action itself against the underground groups Irgun and Lehi.

title: Battle of the Bulge
text: Hitler’s last major offensive in the West is meant to break through to Antwerp. After initial successes in bad weather it fails; the Wehrmacht loses its last reserves.

title: Vistula–Oder Offensive
text: The Red Army breaks through the German lines on the Vistula and reaches the Oder within three weeks, about 70 kilometres from Berlin. Millions of Germans flee the eastern territories.

title: Flight of Germans from the eastern territories
text: Millions of people flee the Red Army, often too late and in freezing temperatures, many across the frozen Vistula Lagoon or over the Baltic Sea. When the “Wilhelm Gustloff” sinks on 30 January, over 9,000 people die.

title: Liberation of Auschwitz
text: Red Army soldiers find around 7,000 sick and exhausted prisoners. The SS had previously driven tens of thousands on death marches to the west. 27 January is today the International Holocaust Remembrance Day.

title: Yalta Conference
text: Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin decide on the division of Germany into occupation zones, an Allied Control Council and the founding of the United Nations. The Soviet Union promises to enter the war against Japan; Poland’s eastern border is to follow the Curzon Line.

title: Bombing of Dresden
text: British and American bombers destroy Dresden’s city centre. According to current findings up to 25,000 people die.

title: Battle of Iwo Jima
text: US Marines conquer the volcanic island against fierce resistance; almost the entire Japanese garrison of over 20,000 men is killed.

title: Bridge at Remagen
text: American troops capture the undestroyed railway bridge over the Rhine and establish the first bridgehead on the east bank.

title: Bombing of Tokyo
text: US bombers drop incendiary bombs on Tokyo’s densely built residential districts. Around 100,000 people die in one night – more than in any other single air raid.

title: Founding of the Arab League
text: Egypt, Iraq, Transjordan, Lebanon, Saudi Arabia and Syria found the Arab League in Cairo; Yemen joins shortly afterwards. It opposes the creation of a Jewish state in Palestine.

title: Battle of Okinawa
text: In one of the bloodiest battles of the Pacific War, besides over 100,000 Japanese and 12,000 American soldiers, around 100,000 civilians also die. After the war Okinawa remains under US administration until 1972.

title: Liberation of Buchenwald concentration camp
text: US troops reach the camp, where the prisoners have already taken control. On 15 April British soldiers liberate Bergen-Belsen and find thousands of unburied dead.

title: Battle of Berlin
text: With the attack on the Seelow Heights the last major offensive of the Red Army begins. On 25 April Berlin is encircled; the same day Soviet and American soldiers meet at Torgau on the Elbe. On 2 May the Berlin garrison surrenders.

title: Hitler’s suicide
text: Hitler shoots himself in the bunker beneath the Reich Chancellery, and Eva Braun takes poison. He has named Grand Admiral Karl Dönitz as his successor as Reich President. Two days earlier Mussolini had been shot by partisans.

title: Unconditional surrender of the Wehrmacht
text: After the signing in Reims on 7 May, the surrender is repeated in Berlin-Karlshorst; it takes effect on 8 May at 23:01. The war in Europe is over. It cost the lives of far more than 40 million people there, including around six million murdered Jews.

title: Berlin Declaration: Allies assume governmental authority
text: The four victorious powers assume supreme governmental authority in Germany. The country is divided into four occupation zones and Berlin into four sectors; Austria receives its own four-power administration.

title: Charter of the United Nations
text: Representatives of 50 states sign the Charter of the United Nations, which enters into force on 24 October 1945. The USA, the Soviet Union, Britain, France and China receive permanent seats with a veto in the Security Council.

title: New states in the occupation zones, Prussia dissolved
text: The occupying powers create or restore states in their zones: in the east Brandenburg, Mecklenburg, Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt and Thuringia, in the west among others Hesse, Lower Saxony, North Rhine-Westphalia and Rhineland-Palatinate as well as the restored Bavaria. On 25 February 1947 the Allied Control Council formally dissolves the state of Prussia, which had comprised about three fifths of the Reich.

title: First atomic bomb test
text: As part of the Manhattan Project the USA detonates the first atomic bomb in the New Mexico desert. At Potsdam President Truman hints to Stalin that the USA possesses a new weapon.

title: Potsdam Conference
text: Truman, Stalin and Churchill (from 28 July Attlee) lay down the principles of occupation policy: demilitarisation, denazification, democratisation, decentralisation. The territories east of the Oder and Neisse come under Polish administration, northern East Prussia under Soviet administration. The “transfer” of the German population from Poland, Czechoslovakia and Hungary is approved – in total 12 to 14 million Germans lose their homeland.

title: Atomic bomb on Hiroshima
text: A US bomber drops the first atomic bomb used in war. By the end of 1945 around 140,000 people in Hiroshima have died as a result.
wiki: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki

title: Atomic bomb on Nagasaki – Soviet attack in Manchuria
text: A second atomic bomb destroys Nagasaki, and around 70,000 people die by the end of the year. The same day the Soviet Union attacks the Japanese Kwantung Army in Manchuria.
wiki: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki

title: Indonesia declares independence
text: Two days after Japan’s capitulation Sukarno and Mohammad Hatta proclaim the Republic of Indonesia. The Netherlands tries to regain its colony militarily and recognises independence only at the end of 1949.

title: Surrender of Japan
text: Aboard the battleship “Missouri” Japan signs the surrender. The Second World War, which cost 60 to 70 million lives worldwide, is over. The same day Ho Chi Minh proclaims the Democratic Republic of Vietnam in Hanoi.

title: Nuremberg trial of the major war criminals
text: An International Military Tribunal of the four victorious powers tries 24 leading representatives of the Nazi regime. Twelve are sentenced to death. For the first time, crimes against peace and against humanity are prosecuted before an international court.

title: Churchill speaks of the “Iron Curtain”
text: In a speech in Fulton Winston Churchill warns that from Stettin on the Baltic to Trieste on the Adriatic an “iron curtain” has descended across the continent. The speech becomes a symbol of the beginning division of Europe.

title: Forced merger of KPD and SPD into the SED
text: In the Soviet occupation zone the KPD and SPD are merged under pressure into the Socialist Unity Party of Germany. The SED becomes the state party of the later GDR.
wiki: Forced merger of the Communist Party of Germany and Social Democratic Party of Germany

title: King David Hotel bombing
text: The Zionist underground organisation Irgun blows up a wing of the hotel housing the British Mandate administration and military headquarters. 91 people die, British, Arabs and Jews.

title: First Indochina War
text: The Viet Minh under Ho Chi Minh fight against the return of French colonial rule. The war increasingly becomes part of the Cold War: China supports the Viet Minh, and the USA finances a large part of the French war costs.

title: Bizone: American and British zones merge
text: The American and British zones form a joint economic area. An Economic Council in Frankfurt am Main, active from June 1947, becomes the forerunner of a West German parliament. In 1949 the French zone joins (“Trizone”); the Unified Economic Area becomes the starting point of the Federal Republic.

title: Truman Doctrine
text: President Harry S. Truman declares before Congress that the USA will support “free peoples” against subjugation by armed minorities or outside pressure – initially Greece and Turkey. The policy of containment of communism begins.

title: Announcement of the Marshall Plan
text: US Secretary of State George C. Marshall announces a reconstruction programme for Europe. The Soviet Union declines participation for itself and the states it controls. By 1952 around 13 billion dollars flow, also into the western zones of Germany.

title: The “Exodus” is turned away
text: The British navy boards the ship with around 4,500 Holocaust survivors off the coast of Palestine and sends the passengers back to Europe, finally to British-occupied Germany at Hamburg. The case causes outrage worldwide and increases pressure on Britain.

title: Independence and partition of India
text: British India is divided into the independent states of India and Pakistan. In mass flight and violence between Hindus, Muslims and Sikhs, 10 to 15 million people are displaced and up to a million die. A war over Kashmir breaks out the same year.

title: UN Partition Plan for Palestine
text: The UN General Assembly decides to partition the British Mandate territory into a Jewish and an Arab state, with Jerusalem to be internationalised. The Jewish side agrees, the Arab states reject it; a civil war follows.
wiki: United Nations Partition Plan for Palestine

title: Civil war in Mandatory Palestine
text: The day after the UN partition decision, fighting begins between Jewish and Arab militias. By the end of the Mandate it escalates into civil war; already in this phase hundreds of thousands of Arabs flee or are expelled.

title: Communist takeover in Czechoslovakia
text: After the resignation of non-communist ministers, the KSČ forces a government dominated by it through mass demonstrations and armed militias. Czechoslovakia becomes part of the Soviet sphere of influence.

title: Deir Yassin massacre
text: Fighters of the underground organisations Irgun and Lehi attack the Arab village west of Jerusalem and kill over 100 inhabitants, including many women and children. The news spreads fear and accelerates the flight of the Arab population.

title: Attack on the Hadassah convoy
text: Arab fighters attack a convoy to the Hadassah hospital on Mount Scopus. 78 people are killed, mainly doctors, nurses and patients.

title: Founding of Israel and the Palestine War
text: David Ben-Gurion proclaims the State of Israel. The next day Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Lebanon and Iraq attack. Israel holds its ground and enlarges its territory; around 700,000 Palestinians flee or are expelled (Nakba). Gaza comes under Egyptian, the West Bank under Jordanian control.

title: Nakba: flight and expulsion of the Palestinians
text: During the war around 700,000 Palestinians flee or are expelled by Israeli troops, about half of the Arab population of the Mandate territory. Hundreds of villages are destroyed or resettled, and Israel refuses their return. The refugees and their descendants still live today largely in camps in Gaza, the West Bank, Jordan, Lebanon and Syria. Palestinians commemorate it as the “Nakba” (catastrophe).

title: Currency reform in the western zones
text: The Deutsche Mark is introduced in the three western occupation zones; shop windows fill overnight. The Soviet Union responds with its own currency reform and the blockade of West Berlin.

title: Berlin Blockade and Airlift
text: The Soviet Union closes all land and water routes to West Berlin. American and British aircraft supply the city for almost a year by airlift with a total of over 2.3 million tonnes of goods (“raisin bombers”). The blockade fails and accelerates the founding of two German states.

title: Tito–Stalin split
text: The Cominform expels Yugoslavia. Tito goes his own way between the blocs and later becomes a founder of the Non-Aligned Movement.

title: Frankfurt Documents
place: Frankfurt am Main, I.G. Farben Building
text: The three Western military governors authorise the heads of government of the eleven states of the western zones to convene a constituent assembly by 1 September at the latest, thereby opening the way to a West German state. At the Rittersturz Conference near Koblenz (8–10 July) the minister-presidents do not want to seal the division: they push through a “Basic Law” instead of a constitution and a Parliamentary Council, which meets in Bonn on 1 September.

title: Expulsion from Lydda and Ramla
text: Israeli troops conquer the two towns on the road to Jerusalem and expel 50,000 to 70,000 inhabitants. Many die on the march in the summer heat to the Arab-controlled areas.
wiki: Palestinian expulsion from Lydda and Ramle

title: Assassination of UN mediator Folke Bernadotte
text: Members of the underground group Lehi shoot the Swedish UN mediator. Bernadotte had proposed assigning the Negev to the Arabs, placing Jerusalem under UN administration and allowing the refugees to return.

title: All-Palestine Government in Gaza
text: Under Egyptian protection a government forms in Gaza that claims to represent all of Palestine. It effectively administers only the Gaza Strip, remains dependent on Cairo and is dissolved in 1959.

title: Division of Berlin
text: An assembly steered by the SED in the Admiralspalast declares the magistrate elected in 1946 deposed and forms its own under Friedrich Ebert Jr., which in practice governs only the Eastern sector. In the Western sectors new elections are held on 5 December without the SED: the SPD wins with almost two thirds of the votes, and on 7 December the city assembly elects Ernst Reuter Lord Mayor.

title: Universal Declaration of Human Rights
text: The UN General Assembly adopts the Universal Declaration of Human Rights without a dissenting vote; the Eastern Bloc states, South Africa and Saudi Arabia abstain.

title: UN Resolution 194 on refugees
text: The UN General Assembly decides that refugees wishing to live in peace with their neighbours should be permitted to return as soon as practicable, and that those who do not return should be compensated. Palestinians still base their demand for a right of return on this resolution.

title: Armistice agreements of Rhodes
text: Under UN mediation Israel concludes armistices in turn with Egypt, Lebanon, Jordan and Syria. The armistice lines, called the “Green Line” after the colour used on the negotiating maps, become Israel’s de facto borders until 1967; Israel now controls around 78 percent of the former Mandate territory. Peace treaties do not follow.

title: Founding of NATO
text: Twelve states of North America and Western Europe conclude the North Atlantic Treaty. An attack on one member state is considered an attack on all. Greece and Turkey join in 1952, the Federal Republic in 1955, Spain in 1982.

title: Basic Law – founding of the Federal Republic
text: The Basic Law is promulgated, and the Federal Republic of Germany emerges from the three western occupation zones. Bonn becomes the provisional capital, and in September Konrad Adenauer becomes the first Federal Chancellor.

title: First Soviet atomic bomb
text: The Soviet Union detonates its first atomic bomb, years earlier than expected in the West. The American nuclear monopoly is broken; the nuclear arms race begins.

title: Founding of the People’s Republic of China
text: After victory in the civil war Mao Zedong proclaims the People’s Republic. The government of the Republic of China under Chiang Kai-shek withdraws to Taiwan.

title: Founding of the GDR
text: The German Democratic Republic is founded in the Soviet occupation zone. Power lies with the SED; Wilhelm Pieck becomes President, Otto Grotewohl Minister-President.

title: Founding of the UN relief agency UNRWA
text: The UN General Assembly establishes a relief agency for Palestinian refugees. From 1950 it runs schools, health centres and camps in Gaza, the West Bank, Jordan, Syria and Lebanon.

title: Jerusalem becomes Israel’s capital
text: The Knesset decides to move its seat to West Jerusalem, and in January 1950 declares the city the capital of Israel. The United Nations adhere to the internationalisation envisaged in the partition plan.

title: Emigration of Jews from the Arab world
text: After the founding of Israel, around 800,000 Jews leave the Arab countries until the 1970s, partly under persecution, expropriation and expulsion, partly by their own decision. In 1950–1952 alone around 120,000 Iraqi Jews are flown to Israel, after Iraq allowed them to leave only on condition of giving up their citizenship.
wiki: Jewish exodus from the Muslim world

title: Schuman Declaration
text: French Foreign Minister Robert Schuman proposes placing the coal and steel production of France and Germany under a common authority. In 1951 this leads to the European Coal and Steel Community, the core of the later European Union.

title: Korean War
text: North Korean troops cross the 38th parallel and push South Korea back to the Busan area. UN forces under US leadership land at Incheon in September and advance to the Yalu; in autumn China intervenes. From 1951 the front freezes near the starting line. The war costs over two million lives.

title: Israeli Law of Return
text: The law gives all Jews the right to immigrate to Israel and obtain citizenship. By 1951 Israel’s Jewish population doubles through immigration from Europe and the Arab countries.

title: Landing at Incheon
text: With a risky landing in the rear of the North Korean army, General Douglas MacArthur turns the course of the war. Seoul is retaken, and UN troops advance northwards.

title: People’s Liberation Army marches into Tibet
text: Chinese troops defeat the Tibetan army at Chamdo. In May 1951 Tibet has to sign the “Seventeen Point Agreement” and becomes part of the People’s Republic of China.

title: China intervenes in the Korean War
text: As UN troops approach the Chinese border, hundreds of thousands of Chinese “volunteers” attack and throw them back to south of Seoul.

title: European Coal and Steel Community founded
text: France, the Federal Republic, Italy and the Benelux states found the European Coal and Steel Community – six years after the end of the war, a common institution of the former enemies.

title: Assassination of King Abdullah of Jordan
text: A Palestinian assassin shoots the king during Friday prayers in Jerusalem. Abdullah had annexed the West Bank and had secretly negotiated with Israel.

title: Treaty of San Francisco
text: Japan makes peace with 48 states and renounces Korea, Taiwan, southern Sakhalin and the Kuril Islands. With its entry into force in April 1952 the occupation ends; Okinawa remains under US administration. The Soviet Union does not sign.

title: Stalin Note
text: Stalin offers a reunified, neutral Germany. The Western powers and the Federal Government reject it because they consider free elections under international supervision not guaranteed. Whether the offer was meant seriously is still disputed.

title: GDR seals the inner-German border
text: The GDR sets up a five-kilometre-wide restricted zone along the border with the Federal Republic. Thousands of residents deemed unreliable are forcibly resettled. Only the sector border in Berlin remains open.

title: General Treaty (Deutschlandvertrag)
text: The Federal Republic and the three Western powers sign the General Treaty. It is to replace the Occupation Statute and give the Federal Republic the status of a sovereign state, with the Western powers retaining reserved rights for Berlin, Germany as a whole and the stationing of troops. At the same time the Federal Republic is to contribute to common defence through the European Defence Community. The treaty depends on this Community, which fails in the French National Assembly in 1954; in revised form it enters into force on 5 May 1955 together with the Paris Agreements. The SPD opposition rejects it and sees it as deepening the division.

title: GDR replaces its states with districts
text: The People’s Chamber effectively replaces the five states of the GDR with 14 districts. The state parliaments dissolve and administration is centrally directed; formally the states continue to exist until the dissolution of the Chamber of States in 1958. The reform follows the SED’s decision to begin the “planned construction of socialism”.

title: Luxembourg Agreement
text: The Federal Republic commits to paying Israel 3 billion Deutsche Marks and the Jewish Claims Conference 450 million Deutsche Marks as “reparations”. The payments contribute considerably to the building of Israel; in Israel the agreement is fiercely disputed.
wiki: Reparations Agreement between Israel and the Federal Republic of Germany

title: First hydrogen bomb
text: The USA detonates the first hydrogen bomb with a yield of over 10 megatonnes. The Soviet Union follows in August 1953 with a test of its own.

title: Death of Stalin
text: Joseph Stalin dies after almost 30 years in power. Under his successors a cautious de-Stalinisation begins; hundreds of thousands of prisoners are released from the Gulag.

title: People’s uprising in the GDR
text: Protests by East Berlin construction workers against increased work quotas grow into an uprising in over 700 places in the GDR with demands for free elections. Soviet tanks crush it; at least 55 people die.

title: Panmunjom Armistice
text: The armistice ends the fighting in Korea. A demilitarised zone along the front has since separated North and South Korea. A peace treaty is never concluded.

title: Coup in Iran
text: With the support of the CIA and British intelligence, Prime Minister Mohammad Mossadegh, who had nationalised the oil industry, is overthrown. The Shah subsequently rules in an increasingly authoritarian manner.

title: Qibya massacre
text: In reprisal for a fatal attack, an Israeli commando unit under Ariel Sharon blows up dozens of houses in the Jordanian-administered village; 69 inhabitants die, most of them women and children. The UN Security Council condemns Israel.

title: Fall of Dien Bien Phu
text: After a 56-day siege the French fortress surrenders to the Viet Minh. The defeat ends French rule in Indochina.

title: Coup in Guatemala
text: An invasion organised by the CIA overthrows the elected president Jacobo Árbenz, whose land reform had affected the United Fruit Company.

title: Geneva Conference on Indochina: partition of Vietnam
text: Vietnam is provisionally divided along the 17th parallel, with all-Vietnamese elections to follow in 1956 – they never take place. Laos and Cambodia become independent.

title: Algerian War
text: FLN attacks begin the war of independence against France. The war is fought with great brutality, including systematic torture by the French army, and leads to the end of the Fourth Republic in 1958. Algeria becomes independent in 1962.

title: Israeli attack in Gaza
text: After raids by Palestinian fedayeen from the Gaza Strip, Israeli paratroopers attack an Egyptian army camp; almost 40 Egyptian soldiers die. President Nasser then arms with weapons from Czechoslovakia.

title: Bandung Conference
text: 29 Asian and African states meet without the great powers, condemn colonialism and call for a policy beyond the blocs. The conference is a forerunner of the Non-Aligned Movement.

title: Paris Agreements: Federal Republic sovereign and in NATO
text: The Occupation Statute ends, the Federal Republic becomes largely sovereign and joins NATO on 9 May. In November the first soldiers of the Bundeswehr are sworn in.

title: Founding of the Warsaw Pact
text: The Soviet Union and seven states of Central and Eastern Europe, including the GDR, conclude a military alliance under Soviet leadership. It also serves to control its own members, as in Hungary in 1956 and Czechoslovakia in 1968.

title: Austrian State Treaty
text: The four occupying powers and Austria sign the State Treaty. Austria becomes sovereign again; the troops withdraw by October, and the country declares its perpetual neutrality.

title: Adenauer in Moscow: return of the last prisoners of war
text: The Federal Republic and the Soviet Union establish diplomatic relations. In return the last roughly 10,000 German prisoners of war and many civilian internees return home by early 1956.

title: Hallstein Doctrine
text: After Adenauer’s trip to Moscow the Chancellor declares in the Bundestag that the Federal Government will regard the establishment of diplomatic relations with the GDR by third states with which Bonn maintains official relations as an unfriendly act. The doctrine, later named after State Secretary Walter Hallstein, secures the Federal Republic’s claim to sole representation and exempts only the Soviet Union as a four-power state: Bonn breaks off relations with Yugoslavia in 1957 and Cuba in 1963 when these states establish relations with the GDR. It has been eroded since 1967 and is superseded by the New Ostpolitik and the Basic Treaty.

title: Khrushchev’s Secret Speech
text: At the 20th Congress of the CPSU, Nikita Khrushchev denounces Stalin’s crimes and the cult of personality. The speech shakes the communist world and encourages reform forces in Poland and Hungary.

title: Nasser nationalises the Suez Canal
text: After the USA and Britain withdraw financing for the Aswan Dam, President Gamal Abdel Nasser announces the nationalisation of the British–French canal company. London and Paris plan an attack together with Israel.

title: Hungarian Uprising
text: A student demonstration turns into a nationwide uprising. Prime Minister Imre Nagy announces withdrawal from the Warsaw Pact. On 4 November Soviet troops crush the uprising; around 2,500 Hungarians die, and about 200,000 flee to the West. Nagy is executed in 1958.

title: Suez Crisis
text: After Egypt’s President Nasser nationalises the Suez Canal, Israel, Britain and France attack. Under pressure from the USA and the Soviet Union they have to withdraw – a sign of the end of the European colonial powers’ role as world powers.

title: Kafr Qasim massacre
text: On the first day of the Sinai campaign, Israeli border police shoot 48 Arab citizens of Israel returning to their village after work, unaware of a curfew imposed at short notice. The perpetrators are convicted, but their sentences are soon reduced.

title: Saarland becomes a federal state
text: The Saarland, semi-autonomous under French supervision since 1947 and economically tied to France, becomes the tenth state of the Federal Republic. In October 1955 about two thirds of voters had rejected a European statute negotiated by Paris and Bonn; the Saar Treaty of 1956 regulates the reintegration, and economic integration follows only on 6 July 1959.

title: Ghana becomes independent
text: As the first colony south of the Sahara, the British Gold Coast becomes independent as Ghana under Kwame Nkrumah. It becomes a model for independence movements across Africa.

title: Israel withdraws from Sinai and Gaza
text: Under pressure from the USA and the United Nations, Israel withdraws its troops. A UN peacekeeping force now monitors the border with Egypt, and the Strait of Tiran remains open to Israeli ships.

title: Treaties of Rome
text: The six states of the Coal and Steel Community found the European Economic Community (EEC) and the European Atomic Energy Community. The aim is a common market.

title: Sputnik 1
text: The Soviet Union puts the first artificial satellite into Earth orbit. The “Sputnik shock” shows that Soviet rockets could also reach the USA and accelerates the space race.

title: “Great Leap Forward”
text: Mao Zedong wants to industrialise China in a short time through mass campaigns. Forced collectivisation, unrealistic plan targets and grain exports lead to the largest famine in history, with 15 to 45 million dead.

title: Berlin Ultimatum
text: Khrushchev demands within six months the withdrawal of the Western powers from West Berlin and its transformation into a “Free City”. The Western powers refuse; the Berlin crisis smoulders until the building of the Wall.

title: Cuban Revolution
text: Dictator Fulgencio Batista flees, and the guerrillas around Fidel Castro take power. Cuba soon aligns itself with the Soviet Union – 150 kilometres off the coast of the USA.

title: Founding of Fatah
text: Palestinian students and workers around Yasser Arafat found Fatah in Kuwait. It relies on armed struggle and on independence from the Arab governments.

title: Tibetan uprising, flight of the Dalai Lama
text: An uprising against Chinese rule is crushed. The 14th Dalai Lama flees to India and forms a government in exile.

title: Sharpeville massacre
text: South African police fire on demonstrators against the apartheid pass laws; 69 people die. The ANC and PAC are banned and go underground.

title: U-2 incident
text: The Soviet Union shoots down an American spy plane and captures the pilot Francis Gary Powers. The planned summit in Paris collapses.

title: Independence of the Congo and Congo Crisis
text: Belgian Congo becomes independent in haste. Mutiny, the secession of Katanga and the intervention of Belgium, the UN and the superpowers plunge the country into crisis. Prime Minister Patrice Lumumba is murdered in January 1961. In 1960 a total of 17 African states become independent – the “Year of Africa”.

title: Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human to orbit the Earth
text: With Vostok 1 the Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin circles the Earth once in 108 minutes – another prestige success for the Soviet Union in the space race.

title: Bay of Pigs Invasion
text: Cuban exiles trained by the CIA land on Cuba’s south coast to overthrow Castro. The invasion fails within three days and drives Cuba definitively to the side of the Soviet Union.

title: Building of the Berlin Wall
text: To stop the mass flight to the West – since 1949 around 2.7 million people had left the GDR – People’s Police and combat groups seal off the sector border in Berlin. Barbed wire becomes a wall. By 1989 at least 140 people die at it.

title: Founding of the Non-Aligned Movement
text: On the initiative of Tito, Nasser, Nehru, Sukarno and Nkrumah, 25 states that do not wish to join either bloc meet.

title: Tanks at Checkpoint Charlie
text: After a dispute over checks on Allied personnel, American and Soviet tanks face each other at close range for 16 hours before both sides pull back.

title: India annexes Goa
text: After 451 years of Portuguese rule the Indian army occupies Goa, Daman and Diu in less than two days.

title: Évian Accords
text: France and the FLN agree on a ceasefire. After a referendum Algeria becomes independent on 5 July 1962; almost a million Algerians of French origin leave the country.

title: Cuban Missile Crisis
text: US reconnaissance aircraft discover Soviet missile sites in Cuba. President Kennedy imposes a naval blockade. For 13 days the world stands on the brink of nuclear war, until Khrushchev agrees to withdraw the missiles; in return the USA secretly withdraws its missiles from Turkey. Afterwards a “hotline” is set up between Washington and Moscow.

title: Sino-Indian border war
text: China defeats India in the disputed Himalayan border region and keeps the Aksai Chin plateau.

title: Élysée Treaty
text: Konrad Adenauer and Charles de Gaulle seal Franco-German reconciliation with regular government consultations and a youth exchange.

title: Kennedy in Berlin: “Ich bin ein Berliner”
text: Before around 450,000 people, US President John F. Kennedy reaffirms the solidarity of the USA with West Berlin.

title: Partial Test Ban Treaty
text: The USA, the Soviet Union and Britain ban nuclear tests in the atmosphere, in outer space and under water. After the Cuban Missile Crisis it is the first important arms control agreement.

title: Assassination of John F. Kennedy
text: President Kennedy is shot during a motorcade through Dallas. Vice President Lyndon B. Johnson takes office.

title: Frankfurt Auschwitz Trials
text: 22 members of the Auschwitz camp staff are tried before a German court. The trial, initiated by Attorney General Fritz Bauer, makes a broad West German public aware of the mass murder.

title: Founding of the PLO
text: On the initiative of the Arab League the Palestine Liberation Organization is founded in East Jerusalem. Its charter demands the “liberation” of all of Palestine; at first it is under Egyptian influence, and from 1969 Arafat’s Fatah takes the lead.

title: Gulf of Tonkin incident
text: After a clash between North Vietnamese torpedo boats and a US destroyer – a second reported attack never took place – Congress authorises the President to use military force in Southeast Asia.

title: Khrushchev ousted
text: The Central Committee removes Khrushchev. Leonid Brezhnev becomes party leader and shapes the Soviet Union until 1982.

title: US ground troops in Vietnam
text: The first US combat troops land in South Vietnam; at the same time the bombing of North Vietnam begins. By 1968 over 500,000 American soldiers are in the country. By 1975 the war claims several million Vietnamese and around 58,000 American lives.

title: Diplomatic relations between the Federal Republic and Israel
text: Twenty years after the end of the Holocaust the Federal Republic and Israel establish diplomatic relations. Ten Arab states then break off relations with Bonn.

title: Mass killings in Indonesia
text: After a failed coup attempt the army under General Suharto has suspected communists persecuted. 500,000 to one million people are murdered. Suharto then rules until 1998.

title: Cultural Revolution in China
text: Mao Zedong mobilises the Red Guards against alleged “bourgeois elements” in party and society. Persecution, humiliation and violence cost hundreds of thousands, by some estimates over a million people their lives.

title: Egypt closes the Strait of Tiran
text: Egypt demands the withdrawal of UN troops from Sinai, moves troops to the border and closes the strait to Israeli ships. Israel had always described a blockade as a cause for war; fear of an attack grows.

title: Death of Benno Ohnesorg
text: At a demonstration against the visit of the Shah of Persia, a police officer shoots the student Benno Ohnesorg. The student movement in the Federal Republic becomes radicalised.

title: Six-Day War
text: Israel pre-empts a feared attack and defeats Egypt, Jordan and Syria. It occupies Sinai, the Gaza Strip, the West Bank with East Jerusalem and the Golan Heights. The occupied territories shape the Middle East conflict to this day.

title: Israel annexes East Jerusalem
text: Israel extends its law and administration to East Jerusalem and surrounding villages and unifies the city. The United Nations declares the annexation invalid; the Arab residents receive permanent residency but mostly not citizenship.

title: Biafran War
text: The southeast of Nigeria declares independence as Biafra. The Nigerian blockade leads to a famine with up to a million dead; images of starving children trigger relief efforts worldwide.

title: Khartoum Resolution
text: At their summit the Arab states adopt the “three no’s”: no peace with Israel, no recognition of Israel, no negotiations with Israel.

title: First settlement in the West Bank
text: Kfar Etzion becomes the first Israeli settlement in the occupied West Bank, on the site of a Jewish village destroyed in 1948. By the end of 1991 around 95,000 Israelis live in settlements in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip and around 140,000 in new neighbourhoods of East Jerusalem. According to the United Nations and most states the settlements violate international law; Israel disputes this.

title: UN Resolution 242: “Land for peace”
text: The Security Council demands Israel’s withdrawal “from territories occupied in the recent conflict” and the right of all states in the region to live within secure and recognised boundaries. The resolution becomes the basis of all later peace negotiations; the Palestinians appear in it only as a refugee issue.

title: Tet Offensive
text: North Vietnam and the Viet Cong surprise-attack over 100 cities in South Vietnam. Militarily the offensive fails, but it shakes the American public’s confidence in victory.

title: Mỹ Lai massacre
text: US soldiers murder over 500 civilians in a village in South Vietnam, mostly women, children and elderly people. Its becoming known in 1969 strengthens the anti-war movement.

title: Battle of Karameh
text: A large-scale Israeli attack on Fatah bases in the Jordan Valley meets fierce resistance from Palestinian fighters and the Jordanian army. Although not a military victory, the battle becomes a myth for the Palestinians; recruitment to Fatah grows strongly.

title: Assassination of Martin Luther King
text: The civil rights leader and Nobel Peace Prize laureate is shot in Memphis. Riots break out in over 100 US cities.

title: May 1968 in France
text: Student protests and a general strike involving millions shake de Gaulle’s government. 1968 becomes a worldwide symbol of youth protest and social upheaval.

title: Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty
text: The treaty is meant to prevent the spread of nuclear weapons. States without nuclear weapons renounce acquiring them, and the nuclear powers commit to disarmament.
wiki: Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons

title: Crushing of the Prague Spring
text: Warsaw Pact troops end Alexander Dubček’s reform policy (“socialism with a human face”). The “Brezhnev Doctrine” claims the right to intervene in socialist states. In January 1969 the student Jan Palach sets himself on fire in protest.

title: Arafat becomes PLO chairman
text: The Palestinian National Council elects Fatah leader Yasser Arafat chairman of the PLO Executive Committee. The guerrilla groups take over the organisation; Arafat leads it until his death in 2004.

title: Sino-Soviet border clashes on the Ussuri
text: Fighting over an island in the border river Ussuri shows the deep rift between the two communist great powers. China begins a rapprochement with the USA.

title: War of Attrition along the Suez Canal
text: Egypt shells Israeli positions on the east bank of the canal, and Israel responds with air raids deep into Egyptian territory; the Soviet Union sends air defences and pilots. A ceasefire brokered by the USA ends the fighting.

title: Moon landing
text: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin become the first humans to set foot on the Moon. Around 600 million people follow the broadcast. The USA has won the race to the Moon.

title: Willy Brandt becomes Chancellor – New Ostpolitik
text: The Social-Liberal coalition under Willy Brandt relies on “change through rapprochement”: treaties with the Soviet Union, Poland, Czechoslovakia and the GDR effectively recognise the existing borders.

title: Treaty of Moscow
text: The Federal Republic and the Soviet Union renounce the use of force and declare the existing borders in Europe, including the Oder–Neisse line and the inner-German border, inviolable.

title: “Black September” in Jordan
text: After Palestinian groups in Jordan had set up a “state within a state” and blown up three hijacked aircraft at Dawson’s Field desert airstrip, King Hussein moves militarily against them. Thousands die; the PLO and its fighters are driven out to Lebanon by July 1971.

title: Death of Nasser
text: The Egyptian president and spokesman of Arab nationalism dies of a heart attack. His successor Anwar Sadat later detaches Egypt from the alliance with the Soviet Union.

title: Treaty of Warsaw and Warsaw Genuflection
place: Warsaw, Monument to the Ghetto Heroes
text: The Federal Republic recognises the Oder–Neisse line as Poland’s western border. Willy Brandt kneels before the monument to the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising – a gesture that goes around the world.

title: Worker protests on the Polish Baltic coast
text: Shipyard workers strike against drastic price increases. Police and army fire on the protesters; at least 44 people die. Party leader Gomułka is ousted.

title: Bangladesh Liberation War
text: The Pakistani army moves brutally against the independence movement in East Pakistan; hundreds of thousands die, and millions flee to India. After India’s intervention Pakistan capitulates, and Bangladesh becomes independent.

title: Four Power Agreement on Berlin
text: The four victorious powers secure transit traffic between the Federal Republic and West Berlin and regulate visiting possibilities. The Berlin crises are thereby ended.

title: People’s Republic of China takes China’s UN seat
text: The UN General Assembly recognises the People’s Republic as the only legitimate representative of China, including the permanent seat on the Security Council. The Republic of China (Taiwan) loses its membership.

title: Nixon in China
text: Richard Nixon becomes the first US president to visit the People’s Republic of China and meets Mao Zedong. The rapprochement changes the balance of power in the Cold War.
wiki: 1972 visit by Richard Nixon to China

title: SALT I and ABM Treaty
text: Nixon and Brezhnev limit for the first time the number of strategic missiles and missile defence systems. Détente reaches its peak.

title: Lod Airport attack
text: Three members of the Japanese Red Army, on behalf of the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP), open fire in the arrivals hall; 26 people die, including 17 Christian pilgrims from Puerto Rico.

title: Munich Olympics attack
text: Palestinian terrorists of the “Black September” group take Israeli athletes hostage. Two are murdered in the Olympic Village, and nine more die in the failed rescue attempt at Fürstenfeldbruck.

title: Basic Treaty between the Federal Republic and the GDR
text: Both German states agree on “good-neighbourly relations” and exchange Permanent Representations. In 1973 both become members of the United Nations.

title: Paris Peace Accords for Vietnam
text: The USA withdraws its last combat troops from Vietnam. The war between North and South Vietnam continues.

title: Military coup in Chile
text: The military under General Augusto Pinochet overthrows the elected socialist president Salvador Allende, who dies during the storming of the presidential palace. The USA had supported the destabilisation of the government. A dictatorship follows until 1990.

title: Both German states become UN members
text: The UN General Assembly admits the Federal Republic and the GDR together, three months after the Basic Treaty came into force. For the GDR it crowns the international recognition that began after the conclusion of the treaty. A few days later Chancellor Brandt stresses before the General Assembly that the Germans live in two states but continue to regard themselves as one nation.

title: Yom Kippur War and oil crisis
text: Egypt and Syria attack Israel on the holiest Jewish holiday. After initial setbacks Israel turns the tide. The Arab oil states cut production; in the Federal Republic there are car-free Sundays.

title: UN Resolution 338
text: The Security Council calls for a ceasefire in the Yom Kippur War, the implementation of Resolution 242 and negotiations towards a “just and durable peace”.

title: Disengagement in Sinai (Sinai I)
text: US Secretary of State Henry Kissinger brokers a disengagement through his “shuttle diplomacy”: Israel evacuates the west bank of the Suez Canal and withdraws to a line some 20 to 30 kilometres east of the canal, with UN troops monitoring a buffer zone in between.

title: Carnation Revolution in Portugal
text: Young officers overthrow Western Europe’s oldest dictatorship almost bloodlessly. Portugal grants independence to its colonies Guinea-Bissau, Mozambique, Cape Verde, São Tomé and Angola.

title: Ma’alot hostage crisis
text: Fighters of the Democratic Front for the Liberation of Palestine take over 100 schoolchildren hostage in a school. When the Israeli army storms the building, 25 people die, including 22 children.

title: Disengagement on the Golan
text: Israel and Syria agree on a disengagement in Geneva: Israel evacuates the enclave conquered in 1973 and the destroyed town of Quneitra. The UN force UNDOF has since monitored a buffer zone.

title: Turkish invasion of Cyprus
text: After a coup on Cyprus supported by the Greek military junta, Turkish troops land and occupy the north of the island. Cyprus has been divided ever since; the Greek junta collapses.

title: PLO recognised as representative of the Palestinians
text: The Arab League summit in Rabat recognises the PLO as the “sole legitimate representative of the Palestinian people”. Jordan thereby has to set aside its claim to speak for the Palestinians of the West Bank.

title: Arafat addresses the UN General Assembly
text: Yasser Arafat becomes the first representative of a liberation movement to address the General Assembly; he comes “with an olive branch and the freedom fighter’s gun”. Shortly afterwards the PLO receives observer status at the United Nations.

title: Lebanese Civil War
text: Tensions between Christian and Muslim groups, aggravated by the armed presence of the PLO, erupt into civil war. Syria intervenes from 1976, Israel in 1978 and 1982; by 1990 around 150,000 people die.
