title: Khmer Rouge in Cambodia
text: The Khmer Rouge conquer Phnom Penh and drive the city’s population into the countryside. Through executions, forced labour and hunger, around 1.7 to 2.2 million people die by 1979 – about a quarter of the population.

title: Fall of Saigon
text: North Vietnamese tanks roll into Saigon; the last Americans are evacuated by helicopter. Vietnam is reunified under communist leadership in 1976.

title: Helsinki Final Act of the CSCE
text: 35 states from East and West commit to the inviolability of borders, but also to human rights and fundamental freedoms. Opposition groups such as Charter 77 later invoke the Final Act.

title: Interim Agreement on Sinai (Sinai II)
text: Egypt and Israel agree not to resolve conflicts by force. Israel evacuates the strategic Mitla and Gidi Passes and the Abu Rudeis oil fields; American technicians monitor early-warning stations.

title: UN resolution “Zionism is racism”
text: With the votes of the Arab states, many non-aligned states and the Eastern Bloc, the General Assembly declares Zionism a form of racism. The Western states vote against; on 16 December 1991 the resolution is revoked.

title: Independence of Angola and civil war
text: Angola becomes independent, but the liberation movements fight each other. Cuban troops support the MPLA, South Africa and the USA support UNITA – a proxy war until 2002.

title: Death of Franco
text: After the dictator’s death Juan Carlos I becomes king. In the following years Spain makes the transition to democracy (“Transición”).

title: Indonesia occupies East Timor
text: Shortly after Portugal’s withdrawal Indonesia invades East Timor and annexes it in 1976. In the following years up to 180,000 people die from violence, hunger and disease.

title: Land Day
text: Arab citizens of Israel protest with a general strike against land expropriations in Galilee. Security forces shoot six demonstrators; the day becomes an annual day of remembrance for Palestinians.

title: Soweto uprising
text: Schoolchildren protest against Afrikaans as the language of instruction. The police open fire; in the ensuing unrest hundreds die. Resistance to apartheid grows.

title: Entebbe hostage rescue
text: An Israeli commando frees over 100 hostages from an Air France plane hijacked to Uganda by two Palestinians and two Germans of the “Revolutionary Cells”; the hijackers had separated Jewish and Israeli passengers from the rest. Three hostages and the commando leader Jonathan Netanyahu die.

title: Tel al-Zaatar massacre
text: After a siege lasting months, Christian militias, with Syrian acquiescence, conquer the Palestinian refugee camp in East Beirut. Thousands of residents die during the siege and the capture.

title: Change of power in Israel: Likud wins
text: After three decades of Labour governments, the right-wing Likud under Menachem Begin wins the election. The new government greatly advances settlement building in the West Bank.

title: German Autumn
text: After the RAF’s kidnapping of employers’ president Hanns Martin Schleyer and the hijacking of the Lufthansa plane “Landshut”, the GSG 9 frees the hostages in Mogadishu. The imprisoned RAF leaders commit suicide in Stammheim, and Schleyer is murdered.

title: Sadat visits Jerusalem
text: As the first Arab head of state, Egyptian President Anwar Sadat travels to Israel and addresses the Knesset. The visit initiates the Egyptian–Israeli peace process; in the Arab world Sadat is sharply attacked for it.

title: Coastal Road massacre
place: Coastal road north of Tel Aviv
text: A Fatah commando lands by boat, hijacks a bus and engages police in a firefight; 38 Israeli civilians die, including 13 children. Three days later Israel invades southern Lebanon.

title: Operation Litani
text: Israel occupies southern Lebanon up to the Litani to drive the PLO from the border. The UN Security Council demands withdrawal and sends the peacekeeping force UNIFIL; on withdrawal Israel hands a border strip to the allied militia of Saad Haddad.

title: Camp David Accords
text: Mediated by US President Jimmy Carter, Anwar Sadat and Menachem Begin agree on a framework for peace. The peace treaty follows in 1979; Israel returns Sinai by 1982.

title: Start of reform and opening-up policy in China
text: Under Deng Xiaoping the Communist Party initiates market-economy reforms and opening to foreign investment.

title: Islamic Revolution in Iran
text: After mass protests the Shah flees, and Ayatollah Khomeini returns from exile. Iran becomes an Islamic Republic. In November students occupy the US embassy and hold 52 hostages for 444 days.

title: Egyptian–Israeli peace treaty
text: Egypt becomes the first Arab state to recognise Israel; in return Israel gradually returns Sinai by 1982. The Arab League expels Egypt and moves its seat to Tunis. The agreed autonomy for the Palestinians does not materialise.

title: Return of El Arish
text: With the handover of the provincial capital of North Sinai to Egypt, the Israeli withdrawal under the peace treaty begins; by January 1980 two thirds of the peninsula follow.

title: Revolution in Nicaragua
text: The Sandinistas overthrow dictator Anastasio Somoza. In the 1980s the USA finances the Contra rebels against the new government.

title: NATO Double-Track Decision
text: In response to Soviet SS-20 missiles NATO announces the deployment of Pershing II missiles and cruise missiles in Western Europe if negotiations fail. A broad peace movement emerges in the Federal Republic.

title: Soviet intervention in Afghanistan
text: Soviet troops march into Afghanistan to support the communist government. The war against the mujahideen, supported by the USA, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, lasts almost ten years and costs over a million Afghans their lives. Détente is at an end.

title: Jerusalem Law
text: The Knesset declares “complete and united Jerusalem” the capital of Israel. The UN Security Council declares the law null and void (Resolution 478); most states that still had embassies in Jerusalem move them to Tel Aviv.

title: Gdańsk Agreement – founding of Solidarity
text: After weeks of strikes the Polish government recognises free trade unions. Solidarity under Lech Wałęsa gains around ten million members – the largest independent mass movement in the Eastern Bloc.

title: First Gulf War: Iraq against Iran
text: Iraq under Saddam Hussein attacks Iran. In the eight-year war of attrition, also involving poison gas, hundreds of thousands of soldiers and civilians die.

title: Israel destroys the Iraqi Osirak reactor
text: Israeli fighter aircraft bomb the almost completed nuclear reactor to block Iraq’s path to the atomic bomb. The UN Security Council unanimously condemns the attack.

title: Assassination of Sadat
text: Islamist officers shoot the Egyptian president during a military parade, also because of the peace treaty with Israel. His successor Hosni Mubarak keeps the peace.

title: Martial law in Poland
text: General Wojciech Jaruzelski declares martial law, Solidarity is banned, and thousands of opposition members are interned.

title: Golan Heights Law
text: Israel places the Golan Heights, conquered in 1967, under its law and administration, in effect an annexation. The UN Security Council declares it null and void in Resolution 497.

title: Falklands War
text: Argentina occupies the British Falkland Islands and South Georgia. A British fleet retakes the islands; the defeat accelerates the end of the Argentine military dictatorship.

title: Israel completely evacuates Sinai
text: Israel returns the last third of the peninsula. The army evacuates the settlement of Yamit against the resistance of settlers and demolishes it – a precedent for later evacuations. The border strip at Taba is disputed until 1989.

title: Lebanon War
text: After an assassination attempt on the Israeli ambassador in London, Israel invades Lebanon to crush the PLO and besieges West Beirut for weeks. In August Arafat and over 10,000 PLO fighters leave the city, and the leadership goes to Tunis. Thousands of civilians die; in Israel the war is fiercely controversial.

title: Sabra and Shatila massacre
text: After the assassination of president-elect Bashir Gemayel, Christian Phalange militias murder hundreds, by some estimates over 2,000 Palestinian and Lebanese civilians in the refugee camps surrounded by the Israeli army. An Israeli commission of inquiry assigns Defence Minister Ariel Sharon indirect responsibility; he has to give up his office.

title: Attacks on the peacekeeping force in Beirut
text: Suicide bombers blow up the quarters of American and French soldiers of the multinational peacekeeping force; 241 US soldiers and 58 French paratroopers die. The peacekeeping force withdraws from Lebanon in 1984.

title: NATO exercise “Able Archer 83”
text: A NATO command-post exercise simulates a nuclear war. The Soviet leadership considers a real attack possible and puts parts of its armed forces on alert – one of the most dangerous situations of the Cold War.

title: Bundestag approves the deployment of new missiles
text: Despite mass protests by the peace movement, the Bundestag approves the stationing of American intermediate-range missiles. The first Pershing II arrive shortly afterwards.

title: Hezbollah goes public
text: The Shiite militia, which has emerged since 1982 with Iranian help, publishes its programme. It fights the Israeli occupation of southern Lebanon and becomes the strongest armed force in the country.

title: Mikhail Gorbachev becomes General Secretary
text: The 54-year-old Gorbachev takes over the leadership of the CPSU. With “glasnost” (openness) and “perestroika” (restructuring) he wants to reform the Soviet Union; in foreign policy he relies on disarmament.

title: Withdrawal into the “Security Zone”
text: Israel withdraws its troops from most of Lebanon but, together with the South Lebanon Army, keeps a 10 to 20-kilometre-wide border strip occupied. Israel evacuates the zone only in May 2000.

title: Air raid on the PLO headquarters in Tunis
text: In retaliation for the murder of three Israelis in Cyprus, Israeli fighter aircraft bomb the PLO headquarters in Tunisia; around 60 people die.

title: Hijacking of the “Achille Lauro”
text: A commando of the Palestine Liberation Front hijacks the Italian cruise ship and murders the wheelchair-bound Jewish American Leon Klinghoffer.

title: Reagan–Gorbachev summit in Geneva
text: For the first time in six years the heads of state of the superpowers meet. They declare that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought.

title: Chernobyl nuclear disaster
text: A reactor explodes at the Chernobyl nuclear power plant. Radioactive clouds drift over large parts of Europe. The Soviet leadership’s hesitant information policy damages trust in the system and promotes glasnost.

title: Reagan: “Mr. Gorbachev, tear down this wall!”
text: In a speech at the Brandenburg Gate, US President Ronald Reagan calls on the Soviet leader to tear down the Wall.

title: Erich Honecker visits the Federal Republic
text: As the first Chairman of the GDR Council of State, Honecker is received in Bonn with military honours – the high point of the GDR’s recognition.

title: INF Treaty
text: Reagan and Gorbachev agree to destroy all land-based intermediate-range missiles. For the first time an entire class of weapons is abolished.

title: Start of the First Intifada
text: In the Gaza Strip and the West Bank an uprising of the Palestinian population against the Israeli occupation begins and lasts until 1993.

title: Founding of Hamas
text: At the start of the Intifada Hamas emerges from the Muslim Brotherhood in the Gaza Strip. Its 1988 charter rejects any recognition of Israel and contains antisemitic statements; through attacks it becomes a rival of the PLO.

title: Assassination of Abu Jihad
text: An Israeli commando shoots in Tunis the military chief of Fatah and Arafat’s deputy, regarded as the organiser of the Intifada.

title: Jordan renounces the West Bank
text: King Hussein gives up all legal and administrative ties of Jordan to the West Bank and leaves the representation of the Palestinians to the PLO.

title: Proclamation of the State of Palestine
text: The Palestinian National Council proclaims an independent State of Palestine in Algiers with Jerusalem as its capital, thereby indirectly accepting UN Resolutions 181 and 242. By 1989 almost 90 states recognise the state, including the Soviet Union and the GDR, but not the Federal Republic and the USA.

title: Arafat renounces terrorism
text: At a press conference Arafat recognises Israel’s right to exist and renounces terrorism. The USA then begins official talks with the PLO for the first time.

title: Round Table in Poland
text: Government and opposition negotiate partially free elections. In the election on 4 June Solidarity wins almost all the freely contested seats; in August Tadeusz Mazowiecki becomes the first non-communist head of government in the Eastern Bloc.

title: Last Soviet troops leave Afghanistan
text: With the withdrawal across the bridge at Termez the Soviet intervention ends. Afghanistan sinks into civil war.

title: Hungary begins dismantling the border fence
text: Hungary dismantles the barrier installations on the border with Austria; on 27 June Foreign Ministers Gyula Horn and Alois Mock symbolically cut the barbed wire. The Iron Curtain gets a hole.

title: Tiananmen Square massacre
text: After weeks of protests for democracy, the Chinese leadership has the army crush the demonstrations in Beijing. Hundreds, possibly thousands of people are killed. The same day the first partially free elections take place in Poland.

title: Pan-European Picnic
text: At a peace event on the Austrian–Hungarian border a gate is opened for three hours. Around 600 East German citizens use the opportunity to flee to the West.

title: Baltic Way
place: From Tallinn via Riga to Vilnius
text: On the 50th anniversary of the Hitler–Stalin Pact around two million people form a 600-kilometre human chain through Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania and demand independence.

title: Hungary opens the border for GDR refugees
text: Hungary lets the thousands of East German citizens waiting in camps leave unhindered for Austria. By the end of September around 25,000 people flee.

title: Genscher at the Prague embassy
text: From the balcony of the West German embassy, Foreign Minister Hans-Dietrich Genscher announces to the roughly 4,000 refugees on the grounds that they may leave for the Federal Republic.

title: Monday demonstration in Leipzig
text: Around 70,000 people march around the Leipzig Ring chanting “We are the people!”. Despite preparations the state does not intervene – the breakthrough of the Peaceful Revolution.

title: Honecker resigns
text: The SED Central Committee relieves Erich Honecker, at the head of the party since 1971, of the post of General Secretary, officially for health reasons; the Politburo had decided on his removal the day before. Egon Krenz becomes his successor. Monday demonstrations and the wave of refugees have put the leadership under pressure. The announced “Wende” does not stop the protests: on 4 November hundreds of thousands demonstrate on Alexanderplatz.

title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
text: After a misleading announcement of new travel rules by Günter Schabowski, thousands of East Berliners stream to the border crossings. At the Bornholmer Straße crossing the officer on duty opens the barrier at 11:30 p.m. During the night people from East and West celebrate on the Wall.

title: Velvet Revolution
text: After the crushing of a student demonstration, hundreds of thousands protest. The communist leadership resigns; at the end of December Václav Havel becomes president.

title: Kohl’s Ten-Point Plan
text: In the Bundestag budget debate Chancellor Helmut Kohl unexpectedly presents a plan leading, via a treaty community and confederative structures, to a federation, that is a federal order in Germany, as soon as the GDR has a democratically legitimised government. Paris, London and Foreign Minister Genscher had not been informed and react with irritation; only Washington knew the wording shortly beforehand.

title: Malta Summit
text: George H. W. Bush and Mikhail Gorbachev meet on a ship off Malta. Gorbachev declares that the Soviet Union will never again regard the USA as an enemy – the meeting is regarded as the symbolic end of the Cold War.

title: Revolution in Romania
text: Protests in Timișoara spread to Bucharest. It is the only upheaval in the Eastern Bloc that turns bloody: over 1,000 people die. Dictator Nicolae Ceaușescu and his wife are shot on 25 December after a summary trial.

title: Mass immigration from the Soviet Union
text: After the easing of Soviet emigration rules, around 330,000 Jews come from the Soviet Union to Israel in 1990 and 1991 alone, almost a million by the end of the 1990s. The immigration changes Israeli society lastingly.

title: Release of Nelson Mandela
text: After 27 years in prison Nelson Mandela is released. President de Klerk had previously lifted the ban on the ANC; negotiations on ending apartheid begin.

title: Lithuania declares independence
text: Lithuania becomes the first Soviet republic to declare the restoration of its independence. The Soviet Union responds with an economic blockade.
wiki: Act of the Re-Establishment of the State of Lithuania

title: First free People’s Chamber election
text: In the GDR’s first free election the CDU-led “Alliance for Germany” wins around 48 percent, with turnout above 93 percent. The result is seen as a vote for rapid accession to the Federal Republic. Lothar de Maizière subsequently leads a grand coalition of the Alliance, SPD and Liberals.

title: Namibia becomes independent
text: After more than 70 years of South African rule and a long liberation struggle by SWAPO, Namibia becomes independent – as Africa’s last colony.

title: Monetary, Economic and Social Union
text: With the state treaty signed in Bonn on 18 May, the Deutsche Mark becomes the sole legal tender in the GDR. Wages, salaries and pensions are converted 1:1, savings 1:1 up to 2,000, 4,000 or 6,000 marks depending on age, and above that, like most other claims and debts, 2:1. The GDR adopts the social market economy and the West German social system; its enterprises suddenly face competition, and many quickly collapse.
wiki: Treaty Establishing a Monetary, Economic and Social Union between the German Democratic Republic and the Federal Republic of Germany

title: Iraq occupies Kuwait – Second Gulf War
text: Iraq annexes Kuwait. With a UN mandate a coalition led by the USA liberates the country in early 1991. For the first time the USA and the Soviet Union act together in the Security Council.

title: Unification Treaty
text: Wolfgang Schäuble and Günther Krause sign the Unification Treaty. It regulates the GDR’s accession on 3 October, decided by the People’s Chamber on 23 August: the GDR becomes the five states of Brandenburg, Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt and Thuringia again; Berlin becomes the capital.

title: Two Plus Four Treaty
text: The two German states and the four victorious powers settle the external aspects of unity: Germany receives full sovereignty, the Oder–Neisse border is definitively recognised, and Soviet troops withdraw by 1994.
wiki: Treaty on the Final Settlement with Respect to Germany

title: German reunification
text: The GDR accedes to the Federal Republic. After 41 years Germany is one state again; Berlin becomes the capital.

title: Unrest on the Temple Mount
text: In clashes between Palestinian demonstrators and Israeli police at the holy compound of Jerusalem’s Old City, about 20 Palestinians are killed. The UN Security Council condemns the police action.

title: Charter of Paris
text: The CSCE states declare the division of Europe over and commit to democracy, the rule of law and the market economy. At the same time the Treaty on Conventional Armed Forces in Europe is signed.

title: Bloody Sunday in Vilnius
text: Soviet troops storm the television tower, and 14 civilians die. Tens of thousands of people protect the parliament with barricades.

title: Iraqi missiles on Israel
text: During the Gulf War Iraq fires 39 Scud missiles at Israel in order to split the Arab states from the coalition against it. At the urging of the USA Israel refrains from retaliating; the population seeks shelter with gas masks in sealed rooms. The PLO had sided with Iraq.

title: Independence of Slovenia and Croatia – Ten-Day War
text: Slovenia and Croatia declare independence. After brief fighting the Yugoslav People’s Army withdraws from Slovenia; in Croatia a war begins that lasts until 1995. Independence takes effect on 8 October after a three-month moratorium.

title: Dissolution of the Warsaw Pact
text: The remaining members officially dissolve the military alliance. The military structures had already been abolished on 1 April.

title: August coup in Moscow
text: Communist hardliners detain Gorbachev in Crimea and declare a state of emergency. Boris Yeltsin climbs onto a tank in front of the Russian parliament; after three days the coup collapses. In its wake most Soviet republics declare independence.

title: Siege of Vukovar
text: The Yugoslav People’s Army and Serb paramilitaries besiege the Croatian city for almost three months and destroy it. After its capture hundreds of prisoners of war and civilians are murdered.

title: Middle East Peace Conference in Madrid
text: Chaired by the USA and the Soviet Union, Israel, Syria, Lebanon and a joint Jordanian–Palestinian delegation negotiate directly with one another for the first time. The conference paves the way for the Oslo Accords of 1993 and the Israeli–Jordanian peace treaty of 1994.

title: Founding of the CIS
text: The presidents of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus declare that the Soviet Union has ceased to exist and found the Commonwealth of Independent States. On 21 December eight more republics join in Alma-Ata.

title: Gorbachev resigns – end of the Soviet Union
text: Mikhail Gorbachev resigns as President of the Soviet Union. Over the Kremlin the red flag is lowered and replaced by the Russian tricolour; on 26 December the Supreme Soviet dissolves itself. With the end of the Soviet Union the Cold War is over too.
